title: Minimal Egress Baseline for Private Deployments: Snapshot Restore & Operator Lifecycle PRD
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: PRD defining the minimal outbound network surface and acceptance criteria required to support snapshot restores and operator lifecycle actions in air-gapped / VPC-private deployments. Balances strict egress constraints with operational realities (patching, artifact verification, KMS rotations, and emergency restore).
problem_statement: Customers deploying Redwood Private in high-compliance environments require the ability to perform full cluster snapshot restore and operator-driven lifecycle operations (upgrade, rotate keys, health-checks) while minimizing outbound egress. Current upgrade and restore flows assume broad egress or persistent proxy access; we must define a hardened, auditable pathway that works with scheduled, limited egress windows, pre-seeded mirrors, or physical media without reducing reliability or jeopardizing security/traceability.
goals: Define a minimal, auditable list of outbound endpoints and protocols required for routine operator lifecycle tasks and emergency snapshot restores
Specify acceptance criteria for air-gapped/zero-egress deployments to be supported by Redwood Private
Provide operator upgrade and snapshot-restore flows that work with pre-seeded mirrors and timebound egress windows
Minimize required code/runtime changes by leveraging existing operator hooks and artifact signing/verification
non_goals: Designing new protocols for artifact distribution outside of HTTP(S)/OCI—we will rely on mirror/proxy or physical media
Full redesign of the operator VM/network model—implementation should be incremental and compatible with current operator
Building a customer-managed global mirror service (customers will use internal mirrors or partner tooling)
success_metrics: Verified snapshot restore in a seeded, zero-egress VPC with no outbound allowed for 30 days: 1 successful test per quarter
Upgrade path that requires outbound egress for fewer than 5 minutes per node during a scheduled window (measured in canary runs)
<20% increase in operator runtime footprint for airgap-related features
Customer acceptance in 2 pilot accounts (one enterprise, one regulated) before GA
requirements: REQ-1: Minimal outbound allowlist: define <= 8 fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) or IP ranges that operator may contact during a standard upgrade or KMS rotation; each entry must have a documented failure mode and fallback
REQ-2: Timeboxed egress windows: operator must support a scheduled egress window (configurable per deployment) and fail-safe rollback if the window closes prematurely

REQ-3: Offline artifact validation: provide capability to pre-seed OCI/Docker images and signed artifacts into an on-prem mirror and verify signatures using customer KMS/HSM without contacting Redwood control plane
REQ-4: Offline snapshot restore flow: support restore from pre-synced object storage (S3-compatible) or physical media with checksum verification and replayable audit trail
REQ-5: Signed image policy: enforce image signing verification with configurable policy (fail/allow-unsigned/allow-once) and documented operator behavior

REQ-6: KMS rotation contract: operator must accept externally rotated keys (KMS/HSM) and provide proof of key-rewrap or rotation acknowledgement to admin console without requiring outbound telemetry during rotation
REQ-7: Limited telemetry grace: minimal heartbeat and health check telemetry allowed during egress window; otherwise operator must queue telemetry encrypted at rest until egress restores
REQ-8: Canary sequencing: define a canary sequencing plan for upgrades under air-gap that supports single-node canaries, staged rollouts, and automatic rollback triggers based on health probes
REQ-9: Emergency fallback: support guided manual operator commands and an offline runbook for rollback or hotfix installation using physical media

REQ-10: Audit and provenance: every artifact and action taken during an upgrade/restore must be recorded with an immutable event ID and signed provenance blob that can be replayed during incident analysis
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Given a private deployment with no outbound internet access, providing a pre-seeded OCI mirror in the VPC allows a complete cluster restore from snapshot within documented SLA (restore completes within X hours for production-size cluster)
AC-2: Given a scheduled 10-minute egress window, the operator can fetch and verify a signed image, update a single canary node, and report success or rollback within the window in 90% of test runs

AC-3: Given a KMS rotation performed by the customer, the operator accepts the rotated key and completes key rewrap operations without initiating outbound connections; rotation events are recorded and visible in the admin console
AC-4: All artifacts fetched during a restore or upgrade are validated against an image/signature provenance log; any mismatch causes automatic halt and non-destructive rollback
AC-5: A simulated mid-upgrade network partition where egress is cut results in automated pause and rollback to the last-known-good state with no data loss in 95% of test runs
AC-6: Telemetry policy enforcement: when egress is disabled, telemetry is encrypted and stored locally; on egress restoration, batched telemetry is transmitted and marked in logs as 'delayed'

AC-7: Documentation & runbooks exist and include exact firewall rules, mirror sync checklist, operator CLI commands for offline restores, and physical media ingestion steps; runbook approved by Security and Field Ops
AC-8: Security review signoff and a penetration test report covering mirror endpoints and image verification flow is included prior to GA
implementation_notes: Prefer leveraging existing operator hooks: preflight, image fetcher, and rollout controller to minimize risk
Build a mirror validation utility (CLI) that customers can run to seed mirrors and produce a signed manifest consumed by the operator
Add a configurable egress window controller that gates network calls and provides a dry-run mode
Add provenance metadata to image manifests (build ID, signature, source mirror URL, retrieval timestamp)
Work with Security to define signature formats and verification primitives compatible with common HSM/KMS providers
Plan a 2-stage pilot: internal test cluster -> 2 customer pilots (one with pre-seeded S3 mirror, one with physical media ingestion)
notes: This PRD attempts to balance strict compliance requirements with practical operator capabilities. We expect follow-up tickets for engineering spikes (mirror CLI, egress controller) and for legal/compliance review of runbooks.
Work closely with Solutions Engineering to collect real mirror workflows from pilot customers; metrics from those pilots will shape the final allowlist
If implementation shows large operator runtime regressions, scope a light-weight advisory runbook as a stopgap while engineering optimizes the runtime
